historical_references.reference: In the early Christian era, some Christians replaced the pagan name Saturn with Saturina, as part of the process of transforming the Roman Saturnalia festival into a Christian feast day known as the Feast of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist. This transformation took place around the 4th century AD.

historical_references.reference: The name Saturina is believed to have been also used in the Middle Ages for a religious cult centered around the veneration of the Virgin Mary, specifically in the region of Languedoc in Southern France. This devotion, known as the Saturina or Saturnina, was associated with healing and protection from evil.
